# Drilling for brine, gas and oil (`oil_drilling`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/energy.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Energy & engines (`energy`)
- Deps: helped by petroleum_refining, high_pressure_steam, bloomery_iron
- Core idea: Deep narrow wells are not dug but punched. A heavy iron chisel bit hangs on a rope or string of rods from a derrick and is lifted and dropped again and again (by men jumping on a lever, a spring pole or an engine) while it is turned a little each stroke; the crushed rock is lifted out with a bailer, a tube with a flap valve at the bottom. The hole is lined with pipe (casing) to keep out water and loose ground; driving iron pipe down to bedrock before drilling is what made Drake's well succeed. Oil is found where it seeps at the surface and under the crests of folded strata. Crude oil is of little use until it is distilled.
- Pitfalls:
  - Saying Drake drilled the first oil well in 1859; Chinese brine and gas wells were centuries older and oil wells were drilled at Baku in the 1840s
  - No casing, so the hole caves in or floods
  - Open flames and boilers near the well: gas and gushers catch fire (the Chinese drillers already knew this)
  - Picturing underground lakes of oil; it sits in the pores of rock
- History: mesopotamia: from the 4th millennium BC – bitumen from seeps at Hit used as mortar, caulking and glue; no drilling; china: c. 1st c. BC – percussion-drilled brine wells in Sichuan with bamboo cable and casing; c. 1041 small-bore deep wells; natural gas burnt to boil the brine; 1835 Shenhai well reaches about 1,000 m; islamic: 9th–13th c. – hand-dug oil pits at Baku (al-Mas'udi, 10th c.; Marco Polo); naphtha distilled for lamps and incendiaries; europe: 1846–1848 – first drilled oil well at Bibi-Heybat, Baku; 1854 Łukasiewicz's oil pits at Bóbrka, Galicia; americas: 1858 – Williams's well at Oil Springs, Ontario; 1859 Drake's well at Titusville, Pennsylvania (21 m); 1901 rotary drilling brings in Spindletop, Texas
- Read:
  - Hans Ulrich Vogel, The Great Well of China, Scientific American 268 (June 1993)
  - Daniel Yergin, The Prize: The Epic Quest for Oil, Money, and Power (1991)
